subject: Catchpoint: MAP slip due to procurement hold — proposed mitigation & decision
messages:
From: Clara Ruiz <clara@finedge.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finedge.com>, procurement@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP v3 / go-live timeline

Hi Avery —

Quick update from our side: procurement just put a temporary hold on contract execution while they re-run a vendor risk check. I don’t have all the details yet; they said it could take 7–10 business days. This will push our agreed go-live window past the evaluation gate in the MAP (which had the final acceptance tests scheduled for next Wednesday).

We still want to move forward with Redwood, but this hold means the eval window and the SLAs in the MAP will slip. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 
- extend the eval window by two weeks without restarting the canary?
- provide a short-term credit or invoice hold to keep our procurement team comfortable?

I’ll attach the procurement notice when I have it.

Thanks,
Clara Ruiz
Head of Integrations | FinEdge

Attachment: procurement_hold_notice.pdf
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Clara Ruiz <clara@finedge.com>
Cc: Evan Cole <evan.cole@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP v3 / go-live timeline

Clara —

Thanks for the heads up and for sharing the procurement note. Sorry to hear about the hold; we’ve seen this pattern before. Short answers: yes, we can extend the eval window without restarting the canary, and we can propose a short-term credit to bridge procurement concerns while they complete the risk re-check.

Proposed next steps from Redwood:
1) I’ll circulate an updated MAP (v3.1) that shifts the acceptance window by two weeks and marks the canary as "preserved" so we don’t lose prefix/KV caching.
2) Offer a one-time eval credit equal to two weeks of projected token usage (applied as invoice credit) while procurement finalizes.
3) Schedule a 30-min call with procurement to walk the risk checklist and share our SOC2/architecture artifacts.

I’m looping in a few internal leads to confirm approvals on the credit and to capture this as a short risk entry in our close model.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: FinEdge_MAP_v3.xlsx
From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Catchpoint: procurement hold — decision reqd (MAP slip)

Team —

Forwarding procurement note from FinEdge. Key ask: approve (a) preserving the canary / not restarting eval, and (b) a one-time credit to cover two weeks of eval usage while procurement completes a risk re-check.

Quick summary to help decide: 
- Impact: pushes acceptance gate out by ~10 business days -> likely slippage of committed go-live by 2 weeks.
- Risk: low technical risk (environment already validated), medium commercial risk (procurement wants invoice-level protections).
- Proposed mitigation: 2-week invoice credit (est. $6k) + joint procurement call with security to provide SOC2 and audit artifacts.

I’ve attached the MAP update (v3) and highlighted the acceptance dates. If we approve credit, we’ll apply it as an invoice adjustment to the first post-eval invoice (not an immediate cash refund). 

Can you reply with: APPROVE / DENY / PROPOSE ALTERNATIVE by EOD? I need a response for the FinEdge call tomorrow at 10am PT.

Thanks — Avery

> On Mon, Mar 2, 2026 at 09:12 AM Clara Ruiz <clara@finedge.com> wrote:
> > Hi Avery —
> > 
> > Quick update from our side: procurement just put a temporary hold on contract execution while they re-run a vendor risk check....
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: FW: Catchpoint: procurement hold — decision reqd (MAP slip)

Avery / team —

I reviewed the MAP update and the procurement notice. Given the strategic fit and probability of closing this quarter, APPROVE the following, with conditions: 
1) Approve the two-week eval credit (apply as invoice credit; cap $6,000).
2) Preserve the canary and do NOT restart the eval (documented in MAP v3.1).
3) Require FinEdge to sign an acknowledgement of the adjusted acceptance dates (short amendment to the MAP).
4) Schedule a 30-min procurement + security sync; Laura, please lead and bring the SOC2 artifact pack and the standard vendor checklist.

Operational notes: Dylan, please log this in Salesforce (deal FE-8821) and mark the close plan as "slippage: procurement" with expected close date +14 days. Avery, coordinate the amendment and send to Clara after the procurement call.

Good call on the credit structure — invoice adjustment keeps cashflow cleaner. Keep me posted if procurement extends beyond two weeks; we can revisit escalation for an executive bridge.

Marcus Lin
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
